destination_record.name: Rajasthan
destination_record.tagline: Forts, palaces and desert dunes: royal Rajasthan from pink Jaipur and lakeside Udaipur to golden Jaisalmer, with tiger safaris at Ranthambore.
destination_record.places: Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Jaisalmer, Pushkar, Ranthambore, Bikaner

on.places: Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Jaisalmer, Pushkar, Ranthambore, Bikaner
on.activities: Pleasant weather for forts, palaces and bazaars, camel rides and sunsets on the Jaisalmer dunes, boat rides on Udaipur's lakes and tiger safaris at Ranthambore, which reopens in October. The Pushkar Camel Fair falls around Oct-Nov and the date changes each year. Desert nights turn cold in Dec-Jan, so carry warm layers.

off.activities: Very hot, with daytime temperatures of 40 to 45°C, so sightseeing happens early in the morning and after sunset. Ranthambore can be good for tiger sightings, as animals come to the waterholes. Palace hotels, indoor museums and lower prices suit travellers who can handle the heat. We suggest skipping the Jaisalmer dunes in the daytime.

mid.activities: The monsoon turns the Aravalli hills around Udaipur green and fills its lakes, with fewer crowds and lower rates. Jaipur and Jodhpur see occasional showers and milder days. Ranthambore is closed for safaris through the rains, usually until October, and road journeys can slow after heavy rain.

profile.overview:
Rajasthan, the Land of Kings, is India's most colourful holiday state. Jaipur glows pink, Jodhpur spills down a hill in shades of blue, Udaipur sits on its lakes in white marble and Jaisalmer's golden fort rises straight out of the Thar Desert. Between them lie Pushkar's holy lake, Bikaner's red fort and Ranthambore, where tigers roam among ruined ramparts.

It is easy to travel for families, couples and senior parents, with comfortable road journeys, heritage hotels at every budget and excellent vegetarian and Jain food. Delhi is the usual gateway, and Jaipur, Udaipur and Jodhpur all have airports. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the route around you.

facts.languages: Hindi and Rajasthani (Marwari, Mewari), English in tourist areas
facts.climate: Oct-Mar pleasant, about 8 to 28°C with cold desert nights; Apr-Jun very hot, 40 to 45°C; light to moderate monsoon showers Jul-Sep
facts.flight_time: Chennai to Jaipur about 3 hr by air, some days via Delhi or Mumbai; Delhi to Jaipur about 1 hr by air or 4 to 5 hr by road or train

reasons.title: Forts and palaces
reasons.text: Amber, Mehrangarh, Jaisalmer and Junagarh forts and the City Palaces of Jaipur and Udaipur are among India's most impressive historic sights.

reasons.title: The desert experience
reasons.text: Camel rides, dune sunsets and folk music near Jaisalmer give you a taste of the Thar Desert in a single evening.

reasons.title: Easy for the whole family
reasons.text: Comfortable road travel, heritage hotels and widely available vegetarian and Jain meals suit children and senior parents.

reasons.title: Tigers and wildlife
reasons.text: Ranthambore National Park offers safaris through ruins and lakes, with a real chance of seeing a tiger.

reasons.title: Shopping and crafts
reasons.text: Jaipur's bazaars are known for block prints, blue pottery, jewellery and leather mojari footwear, and Jodhpur for spices and textiles.

attractions.title: Amber Fort, Jaipur
attractions.text: A hilltop fort-palace of sandstone and marble above Maota Lake, reached by jeep or on foot.

attractions.title: City Palace and Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
attractions.text: The royal residence and the 18th-century stone observatory, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with the Hawa Mahal close by.

attractions.title: Mehrangarh Fort, Jodhpur
attractions.text: A vast fort on a rocky ridge, with museum galleries, ramparts and views over the blue houses of the old city.

attractions.title: City Palace and Lake Pichola, Udaipur
attractions.text: A palace complex of courtyards and balconies on the lakeshore, best finished with a boat ride at sunset.

attractions.title: Jaisalmer Fort
attractions.text: A living fort of golden sandstone, with shops, havelis and homes inside its walls.

attractions.title: Pushkar Lake and Brahma Temple
attractions.text: A sacred lake ringed by bathing ghats, with one of the very few temples in India dedicated to Brahma.

attractions.title: Ranthambore National Park
attractions.text: A tiger reserve of forest, lakes and a 10th-century fort, with safaris in the morning and afternoon.

attractions.title: Junagarh Fort, Bikaner
attractions.text: A richly decorated fort-palace in red sandstone that was never conquered, with fine courtyards and halls.

experiences.title: Tiger safari at Ranthambore
experiences.text: A jeep or canter ride through the park at dawn or in the afternoon; sightings are never guaranteed, but the scenery is superb.

experiences.title: Camel ride and sunset on the dunes
experiences.text: A short camel ride across the Sam Sand Dunes near Jaisalmer, followed by sunset and an evening of folk music.

experiences.title: Boat ride on Lake Pichola
experiences.text: A calm evening on the water at Udaipur, with palaces and ghats glowing in the late light.

experiences.title: Jaipur bazaar walk
experiences.text: Browse Johari Bazaar and Bapu Bazaar for jewellery, block-printed fabrics and mojari, and bargain politely.

experiences.title: Pushkar ghats at sunrise or sunset
experiences.text: Watch pilgrims, priests and floating lamps by the lake, with a short walk through the bazaar.

experiences.title: Rajasthani folk evening
experiences.text: Puppet shows, folk songs and dance performances are part of many hotel and desert-camp evenings.

food.title: Dal baati churma
food.text: Baked wheat balls with lentils and a sweet crumbled wheat dessert, the classic Rajasthani meal.

food.title: Gatte ki sabzi and ker sangri
food.text: Gram-flour dumplings in a spiced curry, and a desert bean-and-berry dish, both fully vegetarian and loved by families.

food.title: Pyaaz kachori, mawa kachori and mirchi vada
food.text: Jodhpur's favourite snacks: a spicy onion kachori, a sweet stuffed kachori and a chilli fritter.

food.title: Ghewar and Rajasthani sweets
food.text: Honeycomb-like ghewar, malpua and rabri are found in sweet shops across the state.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Pure vegetarian and Jain food is easy to find, and we arrange meal preferences with your hotels and drivers.

tips.title: Dress for the weather
tips.text: Wear light cottons in summer, and carry a jacket for winter evenings, as desert nights can be close to freezing.

tips.title: Cover up at temples
tips.text: Cover shoulders and knees, and be ready to remove shoes at temples and in Pushkar.

tips.title: Book Ranthambore early
tips.text: Safari places are limited and zones are allocated by the park, so we reserve safaris well ahead of your dates.

tips.title: Plan for long drives
tips.text: Distances between cities are 4 to 6 hours by road. Start early, take rest stops and keep a water bottle handy.

tips.title: Bargain with a smile
tips.text: Negotiate politely in bazaars and check what is genuine handicraft, such as block print, blue pottery and leather.

tips.title: Be careful with offers at the ghats
tips.text: Pushkar's ghats attract people offering paid puja. Decline politely, or ask our guide to help if you wish to take part.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa to travel in Rajasthan. Carry a valid government photo ID, such as an Aadhaar card, passport, voter ID or driving licence, for hotel check-in and airport security. Ranthambore safaris are booked against ID, and names must match exactly. We arrange permits and safari bookings and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations for domestic travel. Rajasthan is hot and dry, so use sunscreen, carry water and drink bottled or filtered water. Take care with street food if you have a sensitive stomach, and carry any regular medicines with you.
travel_info.money: Cards and UPI work in hotels, malls and most larger restaurants in the cities. Carry some cash for bazaars, small eateries, camel rides and tips. ATMs are plentiful in Jaipur, Udaipur and Jodhpur but fewer in smaller towns, so withdraw before heading to Jaisalmer or Ranthambore.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Rajasthan?
faqs.a: Four to five nights covers Jaipur with one other city. Six to seven nights lets you add Jodhpur and Udaipur, or Jodhpur and Jaisalmer, at a comfortable pace. Seven to eight nights suits a full circuit.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: October to March is the best season, with pleasant days and cool nights. April to June is very hot, and July to September brings the monsoon, when Udaipur is green and Ranthambore is closed.

faqs.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faqs.a: Jaipur is the main airport, and Udaipur and Jodhpur also have airports. Many travellers connect via Delhi. We can plan a one-way route, flying into Jaipur and out of Udaipur or Jodhpur, to avoid doubling back.

faqs.q: Will we definitely see a tiger at Ranthambore?
faqs.a: No. Tigers are wild animals and sightings are never guaranteed. Several safaris improve your chances, and the park's lakes, birds and old fort make the visit worthwhile in any case.

faqs.q: Is Rajasthan suitable for senior parents and children?
faqs.a: Yes. Most sights are reached by road, hotels are comfortable, and the pace can be adjusted. Forts involve some walking and steps, so tell us about any mobility needs and we will choose routes and timings to suit.

faqs.q: Can you arrange vegetarian and Jain meals?
faqs.a: Yes. Rajasthan has a strong vegetarian tradition, and we can arrange Jain, vegetarian and other meal preferences with your hotels and during sightseeing.

group_trips.title: Royal Rajasthan Group Trip: Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur
group_trips.summary: Seven days through Rajasthan's three great cities: Jaipur's Amber Fort and City Palace, Jodhpur's Mehrangarh Fort and the Jain temples of Ranakpur on the way to lakeside Udaipur, with a trip captain.
group_trips.overview:
This group trip takes you through the best-loved cities of Rajasthan over six nights, two each in Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur. You see Amber Fort and the City Palace in the pink city, climb Mehrangarh Fort above Jodhpur's blue houses, stop at the marble Jain temples of Ranakpur, and end with a boat ride on Lake Pichola.

All travel is by air-conditioned vehicle, with rest stops on the longer drives. A trip captain travels with the group, and Indian meal options, including Jain and vegetarian, are available on request.

The days are paced with free time in the afternoons, which suits families, friends travelling together and senior parents.

Photo stop at the Hawa Mahal and an evening in Jaipur's bazaars
Mehrangarh Fort and Jaswant Thada in Jodhpur

group_trips.summary: A Friday-to-Sunday break in Jaipur with Amber Fort, the City Palace, Jantar Mantar, Hawa Mahal, the old bazaars and a sunset over the city.
group_trips.overview:
This weekend escape fits the best of Jaipur into two nights. You see the City Palace, the Jantar Mantar observatory and the Hawa Mahal on the first day, then spend the second at Amber Fort, with a photo stop at Jal Mahal and a sunset viewpoint above the city.

With the old bazaars for shopping and the evenings free, it is a relaxed short break for friends, couples and families. A trip captain accompanies the group, and Indian meal options are available on request.

honeymoon_trips.title: Udaipur and Jodhpur Honeymoon: Lake Palaces, Candlelight Dinner and the Blue City
honeymoon_trips.summary: Five unhurried nights for two in Rajasthan, with a private boat ride on Lake Pichola, a candlelight dinner, a couples spa session and Jodhpur's Mehrangarh Fort, travelling by private car.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon pairs the lakes of Udaipur with the fort-top views of Jodhpur: three nights in Udaipur and two in Jodhpur. You travel by private car throughout, start most mornings late and keep every afternoon and evening for each other.

Udaipur brings the City Palace, gardens and a private boat ride on Lake Pichola at sunset. The drive to Jodhpur stops at the carved marble temples of Ranakpur, and Jodhpur rewards you with Mehrangarh Fort and the blue houses of the old city.

Expect a flower welcome and bed decoration on arrival, a candlelight dinner and a couples spa session, all subject to availability. Tell us your wedding date at booking and we will pass it to the hotels.

custom_trips.title: Forts and Dunes Circuit: Jaipur, Bikaner, Jaisalmer and Jodhpur
custom_trips.summary: A seven-night private circuit through Rajasthan's fort cities and the Thar Desert, from pink Jaipur to Bikaner's Junagarh Fort, the golden fort of Jaisalmer, a dune sunset and Jodhpur's Mehrangarh.
custom_trips.overview:
This private circuit follows the desert side of Rajasthan over seven nights: two in Jaipur, one in Bikaner, two in Jaisalmer and two in Jodhpur. You see Amber Fort and the City Palace, Bikaner's Junagarh Fort, the living fort of Jaisalmer and Mehrangarh above Jodhpur's blue houses.

The highlight is an evening at the Sam Sand Dunes, with a camel ride and sunset over the desert. The drives are long, 5 to 6 hours between cities, so the route is planned with rest stops and a late start where possible.

It suits travellers who enjoy history and open landscapes. Dates, hotel category and pace can all be adjusted.

Junagarh Fort in Bikaner
Jaisalmer Fort, Patwon Ki Haveli and Gadisar Lake
Camel ride and sunset at the Sam Sand Dunes
Mehrangarh Fort and Jaswant Thada in Jodhpur
Private air-conditioned vehicle throughout

itinerary.title: Jaisalmer Fort | Havelis | Sam Sand Dunes
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, explore Jaisalmer Fort, a living fort of golden sandstone with shops and homes inside.
Visit Patwon Ki Haveli and Nathmal Ki Haveli, known for their carved facades.
In the afternoon, drive to the Sam Sand Dunes, about 40 km away, for a camel ride and sunset over the desert.
Enjoy a folk music evening where available, then return to Jaisalmer.
Overnight stay in Jaisalmer.

itinerary.title: Jaisalmer to Jodhpur
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and drive to Jodhpur, about 285 km and 5 hours.
Check in at your hotel on arrival.
In the evening, walk to the Clock Tower and Sardar Market, if time allows.
Overnight stay in Jodhpur.

itinerary.title: Mehrangarh Fort | Jaswant Thada | Blue City
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Mehrangarh Fort, one of India's largest forts, on a rocky ridge above the city.
Continue to Jaswant Thada, the white marble memorial near the fort.
Enjoy views over the blue houses of the old city, then spend the afternoon at leisure.
Overnight stay in Jodhpur.

itinerary.title: Departure from Jodhpur
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Transfer to Jodhpur Airport or railway station for your onward journey.

custom_trips.title: Rajasthan Family Holiday: Pushkar, Jaipur and Ranthambore Safari
custom_trips.summary: A five-night family holiday combining Pushkar's holy lake, Jaipur's forts and palaces and two tiger safaris at Ranthambore, with short drives and an easy pace.
custom_trips.overview:
This private family holiday balances culture and wildlife over five nights: one in Pushkar, two in Jaipur and two in Ranthambore. Children enjoy the forts and safaris, while grandparents can take the temples and bazaars at their own pace.

You visit the Brahma Temple and ghats at Pushkar, Amber Fort and the City Palace in Jaipur, and take two safaris in Ranthambore National Park. Drives are 3 to 4 hours at most, with breakfast and rest stops built in.

Meal preferences, including vegetarian and Jain, can be arranged with your hotels. Tiger sightings are never guaranteed.
highlights: Pushkar Lake ghats and Brahma Temple
Amber Fort, City Palace and Jantar Mantar in Jaipur
Photo stop at the Hawa Mahal
Two safaris in Ranthambore National Park
Short drives and unhurried days suited to children and senior parents

itinerary.title: Arrival in Jaipur | Drive to Pushkar
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Jaipur Airport and meet your driver.
Drive to Pushkar, about 145 km and 2.5 to 3 hours.
Check in at your hotel and rest after your journey.
In the evening, walk to the lake ghats and the bazaar.
Overnight stay in Pushkar.

itinerary.title: Brahma Temple | Pushkar Lake | Drive to Jaipur
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit the Brahma Temple, one of the few dedicated to Brahma in India.
Walk along the Pushkar Lake ghats, and visit the Savitri Mata Temple above the town if time allows.
After lunch, drive to Jaipur, about 145 km and 2.5 to 3 hours.
Check in and enjoy a free evening.
Overnight stay in Jaipur.

itinerary.title: Amber Fort | City Palace | Jantar Mantar
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Amber Fort, reaching the fort by jeep or on foot.
Make a photo stop at the Hawa Mahal, then visit the City Palace and the Jantar Mantar observatory.
Spend the evening in the old-city bazaars at your own pace.
Overnight stay in Jaipur.

itinerary.title: Jaipur to Ranthambore
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and drive to Ranthambore, about 180 km and 3.5 to 4 hours.
Check in at your hotel near the park.
Rest in the afternoon, and get an early night ahead of the safari.
Overnight stay in Ranthambore.

itinerary.title: Ranthambore Safaris
itinerary.description:
Set off early for a morning safari in Ranthambore National Park, in a shared jeep or canter.
Return to the hotel for breakfast and rest.
In the afternoon, take a second safari through the park's forest and lakes.
Overnight stay in Ranthambore.

itinerary.title: Departure via Jaipur
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, enjoy a relaxed morning at the hotel.
Check out and drive to Jaipur Airport, about 4 hours.
Take an evening flight home, or ask us to add a night in Jaipur.

custom_trips.title: Rajasthan Budget Saver: Jaipur, Pushkar and Jodhpur
custom_trips.summary: A value-for-money four-night route through Jaipur, Pushkar and Jodhpur, covering the main forts, a holy lake and the blue city in comfortable hotels, with a quote built around your dates.
custom_trips.overview:
This budget route covers three of Rajasthan's best-known stops in four nights: two in Jaipur, one in Pushkar and one in Jodhpur. You see Amber Fort and the City Palace in Jaipur, the Brahma Temple and lake ghats at Pushkar, and Mehrangarh Fort in Jodhpur.

Hotels are comfortable 3-star properties, and the route is planned to keep drives to 3 to 4 hours. It is a good first Rajasthan trip, and it can be extended with Udaipur or Jaisalmer. Prices depend on dates and hotel choice, so ask for a quote.
highlights: Amber Fort, City Palace and Jantar Mantar in Jaipur
Photo stop at the Hawa Mahal
Brahma Temple and lake ghats at Pushkar
Mehrangarh Fort and Jaswant Thada in Jodhpur
Comfortable 3-star hotels and an efficient route

itinerary.title: Arrival in Jaipur
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Jaipur Airport or railway station and meet your driver.
Transfer to your hotel and check in.
Spend the evening at leisure or explore the nearby bazaars.
Overnight stay in Jaipur.

itinerary.title: Amber Fort | City Palace | Jantar Mantar
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Amber Fort, reaching the fort by jeep or on foot.
Make a photo stop at the Hawa Mahal, then visit the City Palace and the Jantar Mantar observatory.
Spend the evening in Johari Bazaar or Bapu Bazaar.
Overnight stay in Jaipur.

itinerary.title: Jaipur to Pushkar | Lake and Brahma Temple
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Pushkar, about 145 km and 2.5 to 3 hours.
Check in at your hotel, then visit the Brahma Temple.
Walk along the lake ghats and through the bazaar at sunset.
Overnight stay in Pushkar.

itinerary.title: Pushkar to Jodhpur | Mehrangarh Fort
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Jodhpur, about 190 km and 3.5 to 4 hours.
Check in at your hotel, then visit Mehrangarh Fort and Jaswant Thada.
Enjoy views over the blue houses of the old city.
Overnight stay in Jodhpur.

itinerary.title: Departure from Jodhpur
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit the Clock Tower and Sardar Market, if time allows.
Check out of the hotel.
Transfer to Jodhpur Airport or railway station for your onward journey.
